description: Chapter summaries the reader shows under a chapter's title, keyed by chapter number, per language. Like section headings they are editorial aids, not translation: written from Open Word Bible's own wording, stating what the chapter is about and nothing more, so every language can say the same thing. They use no reader settings. Every summary is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

1.en: An Amalekite brings David news of Saul's death and claims to have killed him, and David has him put to death. David sings a lament for Saul and Jonathan, mourning how the mighty have fallen.

2.en: David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron, while Abner makes Ish-bosheth king over Israel. War breaks out, and Abner kills Asahel, Joab's brother.

3.en: Abner quarrels with Ish-bosheth and comes over to David, but Joab murders him. David mourns Abner and declares himself innocent.

4.en: Two of Ish-bosheth's captains murder him and bring his head to David, who has them executed. Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, is introduced.

5.en: All Israel anoints David king at Hebron. David captures Jerusalem, the stronghold of Zion, and defeats the Philistines.

6.en: David brings the ark toward Jerusalem, but Uzzah dies when he touches it. Later the ark is brought into the city with celebration, David dances before God, and Michal despises him.

7.en: David wants to build a house for God, but through Nathan God promises to build David a house, a dynasty whose throne will last forever. David prays in thanks and wonder.

8.en: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Aram and Edom, and administers justice. His officials are listed.

9.en: David shows kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake, restoring Saul's land to him and giving him a place at the king's table.

10.en: The king of Ammon humiliates David's envoys, and Joab and Abishai defeat the Ammonites and the Arameans who come to help them.

11.en: David commits adultery with Bathsheba, wife of Uriah, and when she conceives, has Uriah killed in battle. David marries her, but what David has done displeases God.

12.en: Nathan tells David a parable of a rich man who took a poor man's lamb, and says, "You are the man." David confesses, the child dies, Solomon is born, and Rabbah is taken.

13.en: David's son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar. Her brother Absalom kills Amnon two years later and flees.

14.en: Joab arranges for a wise woman from Tekoa to persuade David to bring Absalom back. Absalom returns but does not see the king for two years.

15.en: Absalom wins the hearts of Israel and proclaims himself king at Hebron. David flees Jerusalem, sending the ark back and leaving Hushai to counter Ahithophel's advice.

16.en: Ziba brings David supplies and accuses Mephibosheth, and Shimei curses David. Absalom enters Jerusalem and, on Ahithophel's advice, takes his father's concubines.

17.en: Hushai's advice defeats Ahithophel's, and David is warned and crosses the Jordan. Ahithophel hangs himself, and friends bring David supplies at Mahanaim.

18.en: David's army defeats Absalom's in the forest of Ephraim. Absalom is caught by his hair in a tree, Joab kills him, and the news is brought to David.

19.en: David weeps for Absalom until Joab rebukes him for mourning instead of thanking his men. David returns to Jerusalem, pardons Shimei, receives Mephibosheth and Barzillai, and Israel and Judah quarrel over the king.

20.en: Sheba son of Bichri leads a revolt, and Joab murders Amasa. A wise woman of Abel gives Sheba's head to Joab, and the revolt ends.

21.en: During a famine the Gibeonites demand vengeance on Saul's house, and Rizpah guards the bodies of her sons. David buries the bones of Saul and Jonathan, and his men kill giants of the Philistines.

22.en: David sings a song of praise to God, his rock and fortress and deliverer, who rescued him from all his enemies.

23.en: David's last words speak of a ruler who rules justly and of God's everlasting covenant. David's mighty men and their exploits are listed.

24.en: David orders a census of Israel and Judah, and God sends a plague. David buys the threshing floor of Araunah, builds an altar and offers sacrifices, and the plague stops.
